content_html:
Google DeepMind wants one AI brain to run every robot, and it just taught that brain to use its whole body. It has released Gemini Robotics 2, a family of models that can control a humanoid from its feet to its fingertips. The system can also coordinate several machines at once and adapt to a new robot body in a few hours.

It is the clearest sign yet of what the industry calls “physical AI,” and Wired framed it as a real step toward “physical AGI.” The pitch is simple. The same kind of model that writes your emails is now learning to walk across a cluttered room and tidy it up.

From arms to the whole body

The headline change is control. DeepMind’s earlier robot models mostly moved an upper body to do tabletop tasks. Gemini Robotics 2 drives the entire machine. It can make a humanoid walk, crouch, stretch and balance while manipulating objects in tight spaces built for humans.

In a demo, Apptronik’s Apollo 2 robot heard a single instruction: put the watering can in the green bin on the bottom shelf. It walked to a table, picked up the can, stepped over to the shelves, bent down and placed it. That sounds trivial. Coordinating legs, torso, arms and hands from one prompt is not.

Dexterity has improved too. The model can drive Apollo’s five-fingered, 22-joint hand to tie knots and seal a ziplock bag, and it can run simpler two-fingered grippers on other platforms. “Our goal is to bring AI into the physical world and then build the intelligence layer that can be used by every robot,” said Carolina Parada, DeepMind’s head of robotics.

Three models, one system

The release is really three models. Gemini Robotics 2 is the vision-language-action model that turns what a robot sees and hears into motor commands. It handles the physical doing.

Gemini Robotics ER 2 is the reasoning layer, a high-level brain that plans multi-step jobs. In its developer briefing, Google showed it tracking its own progress on a live video feed. It can call tools like Google Search, and even steer a Boston Dynamics Spot robot to fetch a snack. It also lets different robots work as a team, a wheeled machine and a humanoid splitting a task. It is available now to developers through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

The third, On-Device 2, runs locally with no internet connection. It can be fitted to an entirely new robot body with fewer than 200 examples and a few hours of training. That last point matters, because moving a learned skill from one machine to another has long been one of robotics’ hardest problems.

Impressive, and still slow

DeepMind was unusually frank about the limits. Its own numbers show the gap. Bloomberg reported the system could unscrew a light bulb 92 per cent of the time, but fiddlier jobs lagged badly. The Chosun Daily put the trash-bag tie at 44 per cent and the ziplock seal at 40 per cent.

The robots are also slow. They pause to think through moves a person makes without a second thought. Kanishka Rao, a DeepMind robotics director, said true dexterity remains a distant goal, and that robots still learn far less efficiently than humans, who adjust after one or two mistakes.

This is a pattern across the field. Rival efforts from robotics foundation-model startups, and dexterity work on rival humanoids, keep hitting the same wall. The demos dazzle, but the machines are still far from ready for the home.

Safety moves up the stack

As robots gain the ability to move around people, DeepMind put more weight on safety. Gemini Robotics ER 2 is its safest model yet, it says, better at spotting when a person is close and halting until the area is clear. It resumes only when the space is empty again.

The company also released a benchmark, ASIMOV-Agentic, that tests whether the reasoning model will refuse an unsafe command from the action model, and whether it flags when a task is impossible or asks a human for help. Naming a robot-safety benchmark after Isaac Asimov is on the nose. The underlying worry, machines acting on flawed instructions, is not.

A hardware problem Google cannot solve

There is an awkward backdrop. Google makes the software, not the robots, and the hardware supply is getting political. As Axios noted, the US just moved to ban future sales of Chinese-made robots on security grounds. Many of the bodies this software might run on are built in China.

Google is working with Western partners including Apptronik, Boston Dynamics and Agile Robots, and more than 100 trusted testers. Its rivals are circling the same prize. OpenAI and Nvidia are both building robot models, and everyone is chasing the same idea: one model, any body.

DeepMind is careful to call this a milestone, not the finish line. Gemini Robotics 2 makes robots more general and more useful than before. It also makes plain how far a machine still is from the easy competence of a human tidying a room.

标题变化是控制。 DeepMind 早期的机器人模型大多移动上半身来完成桌面任务。 Gemini Robotics 2 驱动整个机器。 它可以使人形机器人行走、蹲伏、伸展和平衡，同时在为人类建造的狭小空间内操纵物体。

在演示中，Apptronik 的 Apollo 2 机器人听到了一条指令：将喷壶放入底部架子的绿色垃圾桶中。 它走到一张桌子旁，拿起罐子，走到架子上，弯下腰把它放好。 这听起来微不足道。 根据提示来协调腿部、躯干、手臂和手则不然。

灵巧度也提高了。 该模型可以驱动 Apollo 的 5 指 22 关节手来打结和密封自封袋，并且可以在其他平台上运行更简单的两指抓手。 DeepMind 机器人主管 Carolina Parada 表示：“我们的目标是将人工智能带入物理世界，然后构建每个机器人都可以使用的智能层。”

三种模式，一套系统

此次发布的实际上是三个型号。 Gemini Robotics 2 是一种视觉-语言-动作模型，可将机器人的所见所闻转化为运动命令。 它处理身体活动。

Gemini Robotics ER 2 是推理层，是规划多步骤工作的高级大脑。 在其开发者简报中，谷歌展示了它通过实时视频源跟踪自己的进度。 它可以调用谷歌搜索等工具，甚至可以引导波士顿动力 Spot 机器人去取零食。 它还允许不同的机器人作为一个团队工作，轮式机器和人形机器人分担任务。 开发人员现在可以通过 Gemini API 和 Google AI Studio 使用它。

第三个是 On-Device 2，在本地运行，无需互联网连接。 只需不到 200 个示例和几个小时的训练，它就可以安装到全新的机器人主体上。 最后一点很重要，因为将学到的技能从一台机器转移到另一台机器长期以来一直是机器人技术最困难的问题之一。

令人印象深刻，但仍然很慢

DeepMind 对于这些限制异常坦诚。 它自己的数据也显示了差距。 彭博社报道称，该系统可以在 92% 的情况下拧开灯泡，但更复杂的工作却严重滞后。 《朝鲜日报》将垃圾袋领带的使用率为 44%，拉链密封的使用率为 40%。

机器人也很慢。 他们停下来思考一个人不假思索地做出的举动。 DeepMind 机器人总监卡尼什卡·拉奥 (Kanishka Rao) 表示，真正的灵活性仍然是一个遥远的目标，而且机器人的学习效率仍然远低于人类，人类会在一两次错误后进行调整。

这是整个领域的一种模式。 机器人基础模型初创公司的竞争对手的努力，以及对手类人机器人的灵巧性工作，不断碰壁。 演示令人眼花缭乱，但机器还远未准备好进入家庭。

安全性上升

随着机器人获得在人类周围移动的能力，DeepMind 更加重视安全性。 Gemini Robotics ER 2 是迄今为止最安全的型号，据称，它能够更好地发现有人靠近并停下来，直到该区域畅通无阻。 仅当空间再次为空时才会恢复。

该公司还发布了一个基准测试，ASIMOV-Agentic，用于测试推理模型是否会拒绝来自动作模型的不安全命令，以及当任务不可能完成或向人类寻求帮助时是否会进行标记。 以艾萨克·阿西莫夫的名字命名机器人安全基准已经迫在眉睫。 根本的担忧是机器按照有缺陷的指令行事，但事实并非如此。

Google 无法解决的硬件问题

有一个尴尬的背景。 谷歌生产软件，而不是机器人，而且硬件供应也变得政治化。 正如 Axios 指出的那样，美国刚刚以安全为由禁止未来销售中国制造的机器人。 该软件可能运行的许多机构都是在中国制造的。

Google 正在与 Apptronik、Boston Dynamics 和 Agile Robots 等西方合作伙伴以及 100 多名值得信赖的测试人员合作。 它的竞争对手也在争夺同样的奖项。 OpenAI 和 Nvidia 都在构建机器人模型，每个人都在追求同一个想法：一个模型，任何身体。

DeepMind 谨慎地将其称为里程碑，而不是终点线。 Gemini Robotics 2 使机器人比以前更通用、更有用。 这也表明机器距离人类打扫房间的轻松能力还有多远。
